title: Spot mech transitions in TvZ
items: Game Events now show when a Terran switches from bio to mech against Zerg, with the new Factories lit up on the map. The games list and the player summary mark these games too.
The hotkey chart shows every key, fits the screen and names the units on each hotkey.
Send private feedback from the app, with screenshots and replays attached.
Game dates in the games list now show correctly in every timezone.

title: ShieldBattery support
items: Your ShieldBattery games and players now show up next to your Battle.net ones.
Search the games list by player name.
screpdb recognises all of your accounts and lists them under "You also play as". The You button opens your profile from your latest game.
Insights for Beginner and Intermediate players now compare you with the next tier up, so the advice fits where you are.
Progamer profiles show their hotkey habits, and which progamer's hotkey layout is closest to theirs.

title: A new Insights tab
items: The new Insights tab gives Advanced players advice drawn from their own games.
Game Events now catch High Templar, Lurker and cliff drops.
screpdb times the first Mutalisks reaching the enemy base and counts the Turrets waiting for them.
This website replaces the old in-browser demo.
Game Events read more naturally in Korean.

title: Game insights for everyone
items: Every game report now has insights: the turning points, highlighted on the map.
Bases are named after whoever holds them at that moment.
Bots are detected and marked with a bot badge.
Base outlines and chokes on maps are more accurate.
Fixed rare games where screpdb's replay of the game drifted away from what really happened.

title: Skill on the player summary
items: Player summaries now open with a Skill card.
Skill is measured over the last 3 months of games.
In 1v1 games, side by side bars show who was ahead on each Skill metric.

title: Full game analysis for everyone
items: screpdb now replays every game in the StarCraft engine on your computer, so reports show what actually happened on the map, not just what players clicked.
The app links to a video tour, and to a short video on why it is safe to install.

title: Free replay analysis for StarCraft: Remastered (full tour)
Team games and melee: alliances and game events
Left a team game early? See how it ended
Skill tiers for every game, Beginner to Pro
Who's behind the barcode? Player identity
Nukes, Recalls and a clearer Skill tab
items: Game Events show whether each nuke and Recall worked, on maps that are no longer cropped.
The Skill tab puts every metric on one scale, ordered from your weakest to your strongest.
Opening a newer version of screpdb now replaces an older one that is still running.
Fixed: Windows updates failing at the last step.

title: Skill on every player list
items: Player lists show a Skill column, and the Skill chart fits on one line.
Micro actions replace spell usage on the Skill tab.
Game Events show who owns each base and zoom the map in on each event.
Analysis uses all your CPU cores while StarCraft is closed, and slows down again when you start playing.
Games with no clear winner are settled from the game itself, or from Battle.net.

title: The Skill tab
items: Player pages have a new Skill tab: a tier from Beginner to Pro, the habits behind it, and how it changes over time.

title: Game Events that tell the story
items: Game Events now pick the moments that mattered, show how each one turned out, and play them on a map that looks like the game.
On Windows, updates install the new version for you, and fall back to a browser download if that fails.

title: Full game analysis, in Labs
items: Turn on the engine switch in Labs to build reports by replaying each game in the StarCraft engine, and to try an early Skill tab.

title: Install on Windows with one command
items: Install screpdb on Windows with a single PowerShell command.
Simpler install instructions, now also on every release page.

title: Session habits and matchups
items: Player pages show session habits, matchups, and who they faced in team games.
Use Map Settings games played on melee rules are now analysed.
Fixed: some Zerg openers missing early Drones, Bunker unloads counted as drops, and 6+ Fact Expa shown when no expansion was built.

title: Player fingerprinting in StarCraft in the age of AI bots
summary: Can you recognise a player by the way they play, and tell a human from a bot?

title: Drops are not losses
items: Games you dropped from are listed apart from your losses.
In team games, your own result is shown apart from your team's.
Player profiles show how long ago each game was.
The gaming session view is on for everyone.
The "Became race" filter is now called "New race (Mind Control)".

title: See how a team game ended after you left
items: Left a team game early? screpdb fetches another player's replay to show you how it ended.
Badges show who is behind each account, on the player lists too, and replays from progamer events name the progamers.
Your last session stays visible after you stop playing.
Games with no decided winner get their own result instead of counting as a loss.
Fixed: Zerg Hatchery hotkeys being misread.

title: screpdb in Korean, and built-in progamer profiles
items: screpdb speaks Korean. It follows your system language, and you can switch from the footer.
Built-in progamer profiles, with their Battle.net play habits.
A reworked players page with hotkey details, and one search bar to filter everything.
The dashboard is faster.
Fixed: country flags on Windows, and mass disconnect games counted as wins for whoever saved the replay.

title: Who is behind the barcode?
items: A country flag beside every player.
screpdb recognises players by how they play, on player and game pages.
While StarCraft: Remastered is running, screpdb fetches player profiles from it.
A first look at your gaming session.

summary: How screpdb was built, and what AI could and couldn't do along the way.

items: screpdb's first public release.
